# The checks, and why each one exists

<!-- Generated by tools/generate_checks_doc.py. Edit the check's decorator in
     appstore_preflight/checks/, not this file. -->

Every check below states what it asserts and, in one line, why it exists.
Several say plainly that nothing went wrong to justify them and that they are
inference from Apple's documented behaviour. Those are the ones to trust least.

The reasons come from one developer's apps. They are not a survey of what gets
apps rejected, and a check that fired for them may never fire for you.

Checks marked **needs App Store Connect** issue GET requests against the API
and report as skipped, naming what was missing, when no credentials are
configured.

22 checks.

---

## `bundle-identity`

**Asserts:** Bundle id, team and app name agree across configuration, project and build

**Why it exists:**

A ported preflight read a path that did not exist and reported present keys as absent; what was read is established before anything else is trusted.

---

## `version-strings`

**Asserts:** Version and build number agree, and every embedded framework has a version

**Why it exists:**

Apple's server-side validation rejected an archive (error 90057) because an embedded framework's Info.plist had no CFBundleShortVersionString.

---

## `export-compliance`

**Asserts:** The export-compliance answer is in the build, not left for a human per upload

**Why it exists:**

No incident: a missing ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption turns every upload into a manual question, so the check names the plist it read.

---

## `ad-identifiers`

**Asserts:** The built app carries your ad identifiers, not a vendor's sample ones

**Why it exists:**

An uploaded, App-Store-valid build shipped Google's public sample AdMob App ID and no SKAdNetworkItems, and nothing in the build or upload flagged it.

---

## `ad-runtime`

**Asserts:** Test-ad switches, launch flags nothing reads, and how ads get presented

**Why it exists:**

A vendor test banner appeared in App Store screenshots because a launch flag the scheme passed was read by nothing; an interstitial presented under a full-screen cover hung the flow with no callback.

---

## `analytics-wiring`

**Asserts:** An analytics SDK that is linked is actually initialised and collecting

**Why it exists:**

An analytics SDK was linked and configured at launch but logged nothing, because its configure call was guarded on a gitignored config file.

---

## `asset-catalog`

**Asserts:** The compiled asset catalog and the icon key are in the built app

**Why it exists:**

An upload was rejected for a missing icon: Assets.car and CFBundleIconName were absent from a build that compiled and signed cleanly.

---

## `privacy-manifest`

**Asserts:** PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy reaches the bundle and covers the APIs the code calls

**Why it exists:**

No incident of its own: the same mechanism that dropped an asset catalog from a build drops a privacy manifest, which only opening the bundle reveals.

---

## `localization`

**Asserts:** Every declared language is one the app can actually render

**Why it exists:**

An app advertised a second language on its store listing while most of its UI was hardcoded in the first.

---

## `strings-parity`

**Asserts:** String tables agree on keys and format specifiers across languages

**Why it exists:**

No single incident: a key missing in one language renders as the raw key, and a mismatched format specifier crashes or truncates.

---

## `feature-claims`

**Asserts:** Copy that promises a feature the code does not implement

**Why it exists:**

A paywall advertised benefits the code did not gate, while real paid gates went unadvertised (Guideline 2.3.1).

---

## `price-literals`

**Asserts:** Prices written into the source instead of read from the storefront

**Why it exists:**

A paywall printed a hardcoded savings percentage that did not match the real prices, and a fallback price string contradicted a claim made to App Review.

---

## `paywall-disclosures`

**Asserts:** A subscription paywall carries all six disclosures, in every language

**Why it exists:**

A subscription paywall built from StoreKit's display name and price looked finished while missing the period, renewal statement and legal links (Guideline 3.1.2).

---

## `storekit-wiring`

**Asserts:** A purchase that goes pending is still delivered, and an empty product list is distinguished from a failure

**Why it exists:**

With no transaction-updates listener, a purchase that went pending was approved later and never delivered; an empty product list reached the UI looking like success.

---

## `screenshot-sizes`

**Asserts:** Every screenshot is a real device capture at a size the store accepts

**Why it exists:**

No incident: the size table is the only thing that tells a resized or desktop capture from a device capture.

---

## `screenshot-completeness`

**Asserts:** Every language has a full set, in a stable order, and not another language's images

**Why it exists:**

A re-upload silently reordered a live listing, and one language's screenshots shipped under another language's locale.

---

## `metadata-text`

**needs App Store Connect**

**Asserts:** Store text is within Apple's field limits and has no stray leading whitespace

**Why it exists:**

No incident: Apple's published field limits, and a guess that leading whitespace renders badly. Trust it less than checks with an incident.

---

## `store-readiness`

**needs App Store Connect**

**Asserts:** The declarations and the attached build that block a submission

**Why it exists:**

An app had no availability record at all, which is a different finding from zero territories; an earlier usesIdfa failure was invented and is now a warning.

---

## `availability`

**needs App Store Connect**

**Asserts:** The app has a territory availability record, and it is not empty

**Why it exists:**

The availability read answers 404 before availability is ever configured, and an audit that raised on it printed nothing.

---

## `age-rating`

**needs App Store Connect**

**Asserts:** The age-rating questionnaire against what the code actually contains

**Why it exists:**

An app that links an ad SDK and declares no advertising makes a false statement in the age-rating questionnaire.

---

## `review-notes`

**needs App Store Connect**

**Asserts:** App Review Notes say nothing the build contradicts

**Why it exists:**

A reply to App Review repeated stale review notes that denied ad and analytics SDKs the build had since gained (Guideline 2.1).

---

## `in-app-purchases`

**needs App Store Connect**

**Asserts:** The products the code sells exist, are submittable, and are priced everywhere they are on sale

**Why it exists:**

An IAP check passed while examining nothing because the endpoint omits subscriptions; a product read complete everywhere but sat unsubmittable; a subscription priced in one territory returned no products elsewhere.

---
